task: Develop a composite risk index combining tropical cyclone regime shifts and sea-level rise and apply it globally to evaluate end-century mangrove and ecosystem-service risk.
primary_quantity: Composite mangrove climate risk index by mangrove sample and scenario

sea_level_rise.required_treatment: Extract median regional relative sea-level-rise rates for 2020-2100 at mangrove centroids; derive cumulative 2020-2100 rise proxy and normalized risk.
sea_level_rise.related_work_commitment: Saintilan et al. 2023 emphasize relative sea-level-rise rates and a 7 mm/yr stress threshold for coastal wetlands/mangroves.

tropical_cyclone_regime.required_treatment: Calculate historical cyclone exposure/frequency after filtering/downsampling. Use temporal change between early and late historical periods as a regime-shift proxy where model track years allow; otherwise document limitation.
tropical_cyclone_regime.related_work_commitment: Mo et al. 2023 define TC mangrove risk as damage/exposure combined with frequency and highlight regional shifts; Kropf et al. 2023 emphasize shifts in cyclone frequency/intensity relative to ecosystem recovery regimes.

ecosystem_services.required_treatment: Approximate ecosystem-service exposure from mangrove area and literature value (>US$20,000 ha^-1 yr^-1 cited by Mo et al. 2023) because no direct service layer is provided.
ecosystem_services.units: ha at risk and service-value proxy US dollars per year

composite_index_definition: Weighted average of normalized SLR risk and normalized TC regime/exposure risk, with default equal weights; scenario-specific SLR and fixed historical TC regime component.
required_outputs: figures: data overview, main risk maps/plots, validation/comparison plots
limitations_to_state: sampled 10% mangrove polygons, not full global extent
TC future projections not provided; use historical-regime shift proxy and related-work context
ecosystem services approximated from area and literature value rather than site-specific service layers
